title: Season Steps and the Forfeited Night in Free Night Awards Late-Cancellation Valuation
content:
For one of the Free Night Awards forfeited on a reservation cancelled after its deadline, the season changes the stay's protected value as follows. The season recorded on the cancelled reservation prices the forfeited night: a peak night costs one season step more than the standard-season price, an off-peak night one season step less, and a standard night the standard-season price itself. A category's season step is the gap between its neighbouring seasons on the award chart.

The season is the award season recorded on the Room Reservations record of the cancelled reservation, assigned by the hotel's calendar to the arrival night at booking; the category is the award category recorded on that same reservation.

## Season steps of the Ashbury Rewards award chart

| Award categories | Season step (points) |
|---|---|
| 1 to 3 | 2500 |
| 4 to 6 | 5000 |
| 7 | 10000 |
| 8 | 15000 |

## Price of the forfeited night by season

| Season recorded on the cancelled reservation | Price of the forfeited night |
|---|---|
| Peak | The standard-season price plus one season step of the category |
| Standard | The standard-season price itself |
| Off-peak | The standard-season price less one season step of the category |

### Illustrations (hypothetical reservations)

- Category 3, peak: the forfeited night costs the category's standard-season price plus 2500 points.
- Category 5, off-peak: the forfeited night costs the category's standard-season price less 5000 points.
- Category 7, standard: the forfeited night costs the category's standard-season price, with no step.
- Category 8, peak: the forfeited night costs the category's standard-season price plus 15000 points.
